```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
```

```{r example-data, echo=FALSE}
# Small simulated stand-in for the real panel, so this file runs
# standalone. See pca-explained/, treatment-definition/, and
# did-analysis/ for how PC1-PC4, avg_log_reviews, and g are actually
# constructed from the real data.
set.seed(42)
n_counties <- 60
years <- 2015:2023
sectors <- c("Food", "Health", "Retail", "Other")

county_first_treat <- tibble(
  county_id = 1:n_counties,
  g = sample(c(0, 2018:2021), n_counties, replace = TRUE,
             prob = c(0.25, 0.2, 0.2, 0.2, 0.15))
)

df <- expand.grid(county_id = 1:n_counties, year = years, sector = sectors) %>%
  left_join(county_first_treat, by = "county_id") %>%
  mutate(
    county_sector    = paste(county_id, sector, sep = "_"),
    PC1 = rnorm(n()), PC2 = rnorm(n()), PC3 = rnorm(n()), PC4 = rnorm(n()),
    avg_log_reviews  = rnorm(n(), 2, 1),
    event_time       = ifelse(g != 0, year - g, NA_real_),
    treated_now      = as.integer(g != 0 & year >= g),
    # sector-specific effect size, so heterogeneity check has something to find
    sector_effect    = case_when(sector == "Food" ~ 7, sector == "Retail" ~ 4, TRUE ~ 1),
    est = 100 + 2 * (year - min(years)) +
      treated_now * sector_effect +
      county_id * 0.05 + rnorm(n(), 0, 3)
  )
```

## 1. IPW-weighted regression (alternative to the doubly-robust DiD)

```{r ipw-weights}
# Weight construction: model the change in review activity as a
# function of the PCA controls, then weight each observation by how
# "surprising" its actual review change was relative to that model.
make_ipw_treated <- function(data){
  data2 <- data %>%
    arrange(county_id, year) %>%
    group_by(county_id) %>%
    mutate(d_review = avg_log_reviews - lag(avg_log_reviews)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(d_review))

  mu0    <- mean(data2$d_review)
  sigma0 <- sd(data2$d_review)

  cond_mod  <- lm(d_review ~ PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4, data = data2)
  mu_hat    <- predict(cond_mod, data2)
  sigma_hat <- sd(residuals(cond_mod))

  data2 %>%
    mutate(
      log_wt   = dnorm(d_review, mu0, sigma0, log = TRUE) -
                 dnorm(d_review, mu_hat, sigma_hat, log = TRUE),
      log_wt_c = log_wt - median(log_wt, na.rm = TRUE),
      ipw_wt   = exp(log_wt_c),
      ipw_wt   = ipw_wt / mean(ipw_wt, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
}

df_wt <- make_ipw_treated(df) %>% filter(!is.na(ipw_wt))

hist(df_wt$ipw_wt, breaks = 30, main = "IPW Weights", xlab = "Weight")
```

```{r ipw-regression}
fe_ipw <- lm(
  est ~ avg_log_reviews + PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + factor(county_id) + factor(year),
  data    = df_wt,
  weights = ipw_wt
)

coeftest(fe_ipw, vcov = vcovCL, cluster = ~county_id)["avg_log_reviews", ]
```

## 2. Sector heterogeneity

```{r sector-event-study}
# Same event-study logic as did-analysis/, but with county x sector as
# the panel unit, to see whether the effect is concentrated in
# particular kinds of businesses rather than uniform across all of them.
es_sec <- df %>% filter(!is.na(event_time) & between(event_time, -4, 4))

es_mod_sec <- feols(
  est ~ i(event_time, ref = -1) | county_sector + year,
  cluster = ~county_sector,
  data    = es_sec
)

iplot(
  es_mod_sec,
  xlab = "Years since first Yelp review (sector)",
  main = "Event Study by Sector"
)
```

```{r sector-means}
df %>%
  filter(!is.na(event_time)) %>%
  mutate(post = event_time >= 0) %>%
  group_by(sector, post) %>%
  summarise(mean_est = mean(est, na.rm = TRUE), n = n(), .groups = "drop")
```

## 3. Sensitivity to the treatment threshold

```{r threshold-sensitivity}
# Re-derive binary treatment at 60th / 75th / 90th percentiles (see
# treatment-definition/) and compare the resulting effect size, to
# check the main result isn't an artifact of exactly where the line
# is drawn.
run_at_threshold <- function(pct) {
  thr <- quantile(df$avg_log_reviews, pct, na.rm = TRUE)

  first_treat <- df %>%
    group_by(county_id) %>%
    summarise(first_year = min(year[avg_log_reviews > thr], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  d <- df %>%
    left_join(first_treat, by = "county_id") %>%
    mutate(
      treated = as.integer(!is.na(first_year)),
      post    = as.integer(year >= first_year),
      did_bin = treated * post
    )

  mod <- feols(est ~ did_bin | county_id + year, cluster = ~county_id, data = d)
  broom::tidy(mod) %>% filter(term == "did_bin") %>% mutate(percentile = pct)
}

results <- purrr::map_dfr(c(0.60, 0.75, 0.90), run_at_threshold)
results
```
